reason: Conversation 1 gave an honest, hedged diagnosis (start relay/overload most likely, weak compressor possible, uneconomic if so), correctly asked about compressor temperature and age, directed the free condenser-clean/ventilation step first, and advised an engineer to measure current draw before committing money, plus sensible food-safety and warranty notes. Conversation 2 suffered a service outage, never asked about condenser cleanliness or airflow, and after the homeowner explicitly asked for the exact part for their model it offered only generic 'pull the wires off, match colours if possible' instructions without identifying the Bosch part or recommending confirmation first, which is both less safe and less useful. Conversation 1's only weakness is leaning a little hard on 'overheating' after the hot-compressor answer, but it still kept the relay-vs-compressor uncertainty and escalation path intact.
